definitions.explanation: One of the fundamental colors from which all other colors can be mixed — red, blue, and yellow in art, or red, green, and blue in light.
By extension, any bright, saturated, pure color. Often used to describe bold or striking color choices in fashion, design, or nature.

examples.japanese: {光|ひかり}の{三|さん}{原色|げんしょく}は{赤|あか}・{緑|みどり}・{青|あお}だ。
examples.english: The three primary colors of light are red, green, and blue.

examples.japanese: {原色|げんしょく}を{混|ま}ぜて{新|あたら}しい{色|いろ}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Mix primary colors to create new colors.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}、{美術|びじゅつ}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{原色|げんしょく}について{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I learned about primary colors in art class as a child.

examples.japanese: {原色|げんしょく}の{服|ふく}が{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like clothes in vivid colors.

examples.japanese: {南国|なんごく}の{花|はな}は{原色|げんしょく}が{鮮|あざ}やかだ。
examples.english: Tropical flowers have strikingly vivid colors.

examples.japanese: {原色|げんしょく}を{使|つか}った{大胆|だいたん}なデザインが{目|め}を{引|ひ}く。
examples.english: The bold design using vivid colors catches the eye.

notes:
USAGE:
In technical usage, {原色|げんしょく} refers strictly to primary colors in color theory. In everyday usage, it broadly describes any bold, saturated color that has not been softened or mixed — the kind of bright hues found in tropical scenery or pop art.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三|さん}{原色|げんしょく} (three primary colors)
- {原色|げんしょく}の{花|はな} (vividly colored flowers)
- {原色|げんしょく}を{使|つか}う (to use vivid colors)
- {光|ひかり}の{原色|げんしょく} (primary colors of light)

FORMS:
{原|げん} (original, fundamental) + {色|しょく} (color).
